q: The rate of doing work is defined as ____.
e: Power is work per unit time. In SI that unit is the watt: 1 W = 1 J s⁻¹. The rate of doing work is defined as power.

q: The unit for power in SI units is the ____.
e: SI power is the watt. Erg per second is CGS. Horsepower is the British engineering unit. The unit for power in SI units is the watt (W).

q: If the work done is 1 joule in 1 second, the power is ____.
e: One joule in one second is one watt. If the work done is 1 joule in 1 second, the power is 1 watt.

q: The units of power which are larger than watt are kilowatt (kW) and ____.
e: 1 kW = 10³ W and 1 MW = 10⁶ W. The units of power which are larger than watt are kilowatt (kW) and megawatt (MW). Megawatt (mw) is what this sentence is naming.
1 kW = 1000 W, 1 MW = 10⁶ W, and 1 hp = 746 W = 550 ft-lb s⁻¹. 1 kW = 10³ W.
1 kW = 1000 W, 1 MW = 10⁶ W, and 1 hp = 746 W = 550 ft-lb s⁻¹. 1 MW = 10^6 W.

q: In the CGS system, the unit of power is ____.
e: Work is F · s. Power is work per second, in watts. In the CGS system, the unit of power is erg s^-1.

q: In the British system, the unit of power is ____.
e: Work is F · s. Power is work per second, in watts. In the British system, the unit of power is foot-pound per second (ft-lb s^-1).

q: In British engineering system, the unit of power is ____.
e: Work is F · s. Power is work per second, in watts. In British engineering system, the unit of power is horse power (hp).

q: If the work done in 1 second is 550 ft-lb, the power is ____.
e: 550 ft-lb in one second is one horsepower. If the work done in 1 second is 550 ft-lb, the power is 1 horse power.
CGS power is the erg per second. 1 W = 10^7 erg s^-1.
1 kW = 1000 W, 1 MW = 10⁶ W, and 1 hp = 746 W = 550 ft-lb s⁻¹. 1 hp = 746 W.
CGS power is the erg per second. 1 hp = 746 × 10^7 erg s^-1.

q: For uniform motion, $P = Fv$ where $v$ is ____.
e: At constant speed, power is force times velocity, P = Fv. For uniform motion, P = Fv where v is average velocity.

q: Power is not a fundamental concept like energy but it is a very important concept for ____.
e: The fundamental is the lowest standing-wave frequency. Higher ones are harmonics or overtones. Power is not a fundamental concept like energy but it is a very important concept for engineering works.

q: Car engines, water pumps, refrigerators, air conditioners and electric bulbs, etc., are specified according to their ____.
e: Machines are rated by the power they consume or deliver. Car engines, water pumps, refrigerators, air conditioners and electric bulbs, etc., are specified according to their power consumption.

q: Efficiency is another technical term that is derived from ____.
e: Efficiency is another technical term that is derived from everyday usage. Everyday usage is what this statement is using.

q: In physics and engineering, efficiency has a ____.
e: In physics and engineering, efficiency has a precise meaning. Precise meaning is what this statement is using.

q: A simple machine is a mechanical device that amplifies the magnitude of a force and ____.
e: A simple machine is a mechanical device that amplifies the magnitude of a force and changes its position. Changes its position is what this statement is using.

q: Simple machines are used to make ____ easier.
e: Simple machines are used to make work easier. Work is what this statement is using.

q: Nowadays, machines are just combinations or more complicated forms of the ____ simple machines.
e: Nowadays, machines are just combinations or more complicated forms of the six simple machines. Six is what this statement is using.

q: The six simple machines are lever, wheel and axle, pulley, inclined plane, screw and ____.
e: The six simple machines are lever, wheel and axle, pulley, inclined plane, screw and wedge. Wedge is what this statement is using.

q: Mechanical advantage = ____.
e: Mechanical advantage = (L)/(E). Leave the relation as (L)/(E).

q: In practice, friction is always present. It should, therefore, be remembered that some effort is spent in overcoming ____.
e: In practice, friction is always present. It should, therefore, be remembered that some effort is spent in overcoming friction. Friction is what this statement is using.

q: The ratio of the distance moved by the effort to that of the load in the same time is called the ____ of the machine.
e: The ratio of the distance moved by the effort to that of the load in the same time is called the velocity ratio of the machine. The name used here is velocity ratio.

q: Velocity ratio = ____.
e: Velocity ratio = (Seffort)/(Sload). Leave the relation as (Seffort)/(Sload).

q: The work obtained is called the ____ work.
e: Work is F · s. Power is work per second, in watts. The work obtained is called the output work.

q: The work supplied is called the ____ work.
e: Work is F · s. Power is work per second, in watts. The work supplied is called the input work.

q: The ratio of output work to input work is defined as the ____ of the machine.
e: Work is the scalar product of force and displacement, W = Fs cos θ. The ratio of output work to input work is defined as the efficiency of the machine.

q: Efficiency is generally expressed in the ____ form.
e: Efficiency is generally expressed in the percentage form. Percentage is what this statement is using.

q: Efficiency = $\frac{\text{output work}}{\text{input work}} \times$ ____.
e: Work is F · s. Power is work per second, in watts. Efficiency = (output work)/(input work) × 100%.

q: Efficiency = $\frac{MA}{VR} \times$ ____.
e: Efficiency = (MA)/(VR) × 100%. 100% is what this statement is using.

q: It is impossible, in practice, to build a perfect machine for which output work is equal to ____ work.
e: Work is F · s. Power is work per second, in watts. It is impossible, in practice, to build a perfect machine for which output work is equal to input work.

q: Therefore, the efficiency of a machine must always be less than ____.
e: Therefore, the efficiency of a machine must always be less than 100%. 100% is what this statement is using.

q: Ability to retain the original form when the applied force is removed is called ____.
e: Ability to retain the original form when the applied force is removed is called elasticity. The name used here is elasticity.

q: Not only springs but also other objects such as threads and rubber bands have ____ property.
e: Not only springs but also other objects such as threads and rubber bands have elastic property. Elastic is what this statement is using.

q: Elastic limit is a limit, beyond which if an elastic object is stretched, it will not return to its ____.
e: Elastic limit is a limit, beyond which if an elastic object is stretched, it will not return to its original form. Original form is what this statement is using.

q: Robert Hooke, the English scientist, noted that when an elastic body such as a spring is stretched by a weight (or) a force, the amount of elongation of the spring is proportional to the ____ that produces it so long as the elastic limit is not exceeded.
e: Robert Hooke, the English scientist, noted that when an elastic body such as a spring is stretched by a weight (or) a force, the amount of elongation of the spring is proportional to the applied force that produces it so long as the elastic limit is not exceeded. Applied force is what this statement is using.

q: The amount of elongation is also called ____.
e: The amount of elongation is also called extension. The name used here is extension.

q: As long as the elastic limit of a body is not exceeded, the strain produced is proportional to ____ causing it.
e: As long as the elastic limit of a body is not exceeded, the strain produced is proportional to stress causing it. Stress is what this statement is using.

q: In symbols, $F \propto x$ (or) $F = kx$, where $F$ is the applied force (or) stress, $x$ is the elongation (or) strain and $k$ is a ____.
e: K depends on the units and on the permittivity of the medium. In vacuum K = 1/(4πε0) = 9 × 10⁹. In symbols, F ∝ x (or) F = kx, where F is the applied force (or) stress, x is the elongation (or) strain and k is a constant.

q: For a spring, $k$ is also called ____.
e: For a spring, k is also called spring constant. The name used here is spring constant.

q: The unit of $k$ is ____.
e: The unit of k is Nm^-1. The unit written here is Nm^-1.

q: Hooke's law expresses the ____ behavior of materials.
e: Hooke's law expresses the elastic behavior of materials. Elastic is what this statement is using.

q: The work done is stored as the potential energy of the ____.
e: Work is F · s. Power is work per second, in watts. The work done is stored as the potential energy of the spring.

q: The elastic potential energy stored by the stretched spring is also $\frac{1}{2}kx^2$. Thus, $W = \Delta PE = $ ____.
e: Work is F · s. Power is work per second, in watts. The elastic potential energy stored by the stretched spring is also (1)/(2)kx². Thus, W = ΔPE = (1)/(2)kx².

q: Energy is the ability to do ____.
e: Energy is the ability to do work. Work is what this statement is using.

q: Energy exists in many forms and can be converted from one form to ____.
e: Energy exists in many forms and can be converted from one form to another. Another is what this statement is using.

q: Energy sources can be classified as two major sources: conventional sources and ____ sources.
e: Energy sources can be classified as two major sources: conventional sources and non-conventional sources. Non-conventional is what this statement is using.

q: Conventional energy sources are ____ and non-conventional energy sources are renewable energy sources.
e: Conventional energy sources are non-renewable and non-conventional energy sources are renewable energy sources. Non-renewable is what this statement is using.

q: Renewable energy sources are ____ energy sources.
e: Renewable energy sources are sustainable energy sources. Sustainable is what this statement is using.

q: A renewable energy source is generated from unlimited natural sources (e.g. sun, wind, hydropower) and is always replenished and is ____ to the environment.
e: Work is F · s. Power is work per second, in watts. A renewable energy source is generated from unlimited natural sources (e.g. sun, wind, hydropower) and is always replenished and is safe to the environment.

q: The most popular renewable energy sources currently are solar energy, wind energy, hydro energy, tidal energy, geothermal energy and ____ energy.
e: The most popular renewable energy sources currently are solar energy, wind energy, hydro energy, tidal energy, geothermal energy and biomass energy. Biomass is what this statement is using.

q: Sun is the primary source of ____.
e: Sun is the primary source of energy. Energy is what this statement is using.

q: Sunlight is a clean, renewable source of ____.
e: Lenses refract. Light is an electromagnetic wave and also a particle. Sunlight is a clean, renewable source of energy.

q: With the help of photovoltaic technology, solar energy can be used to generate ____.
e: With the help of photovoltaic technology, solar energy can be used to generate electricity. Electricity is what this statement is using.

q: Wind is the natural movement of ____ across the land or sea.
e: Wind is the natural movement of air across the land or sea. Air is what this statement is using.

q: The wind when used to turn the blades of a turbine turns the shaft to which they are attached. This movement of shaft of the generator produces ____.
e: The wind when used to turn the blades of a turbine turns the shaft to which they are attached. This movement of shaft of the generator produces electricity. Electricity is what this statement is using.

q: Hydro energy uses flowing water to power machinery and generate ____.
e: Work is F · s. Power is work per second, in watts. Hydro energy uses flowing water to power machinery and generate electricity.

q: Tidal energy is another form of hydro energy that uses tidal currents twice-daily to drive turbine ____.
e: Tidal energy is another form of hydro energy that uses tidal currents twice-daily to drive turbine generators. Generators is what this statement is using.

q: Geothermal energy is more readily available in areas affected by ____.
e: Geothermal energy is more readily available in areas affected by volcanism. Volcanism is what this statement is using.

q: Biomass is plant or animal material used as fuel to produce electricity or ____.
e: Biomass is plant or animal material used as fuel to produce electricity or heat. Heat is what this statement is using.

q: Biomass can also be converted into other forms of energy such as methane gas, ethanol and ____.
e: Biomass can also be converted into other forms of energy such as methane gas, ethanol and biodiesel. Biodiesel is what this statement is using.

q: The four major roles of a renewable energy are (i) electricity generation, (ii) air and water heating/cooling, (iii) reduction of greenhouse gases (GHG), and (iv) replacement of ____ fuels.
e: Heat is energy flowing because of a temperature difference. SI unit is the joule. The four major roles of a renewable energy are (i) electricity generation, (ii) air and water heating/cooling, (iii) reduction of greenhouse gases (GHG), and (iv) replacement of fossil fuels.

q: Non-renewable energy comes from sources that will run out or will not be replenished for thousands or even ____ of years.
e: Non-renewable energy comes from sources that will run out or will not be replenished for thousands or even millions of years. Millions is what this statement is using.

q: Four main types of non-renewable energy sources are oil, natural gas, coal and ____ energy.
e: Four main types of non-renewable energy sources are oil, natural gas, coal and nuclear energy. Nuclear is what this statement is using.

q: Oil, natural gas and coal are collectively called ____ fuels.
e: Oil, natural gas and coal are collectively called fossil fuels. The name used here is fossil.

q: Fossil fuels were formed within the earth from dead plants and animals over ____ of years.
e: Fossil fuels were formed within the earth from dead plants and animals over millions of years. Millions is what this statement is using.

q: Nuclear energy is produced by using elements like uranium and thorium, which cannot be ____.
e: Nuclear energy is produced by using elements like uranium and thorium, which cannot be replenished. Replenished is what this statement is using.

q: Nuclear energy can be used to generate electricity by means of nuclear ____.
e: Nuclear energy can be used to generate electricity by means of nuclear fission. Fission is what this statement is using.

q: In a nuclear reactor, the nuclear fuel is used to carry out sustained fission chain reaction to produce electricity at a ____ rate.
e: In a nuclear reactor, the nuclear fuel is used to carry out sustained fission chain reaction to produce electricity at a controlled rate. Controlled is what this statement is using.
